observed_contact_surfaces.surface: Exposed graphics-card PCB back and component-populated free-edge region. These are visible but are not selected as jaw contacts.

inferred_contact_surfaces.surface: Potential opposing faces of the graphics-card cooler/shroud
inferred_contact_surfaces.basis: HISTORICAL1987 shows a substantial cooler/shroud beneath the PCB. CURRENT2115 does not resolve a reliable mechanical contact patch or its opposing face.
inferred_contact_surfaces.assumption: The historical cooler/shroud remains attached; its accessible gripping surfaces and load-bearing suitability are unverified.

approach_description: Use a bounded open-hand withdrawal carrying the wrist camera, rather than another external camera sweep. Seek parallax past the PCB free edge and right fingertip, which obscure the adjacent cooler/shroud region in the current wrist image. Withdraw toward the open case top with a small component away from the card into the foreground gap between the fingers. Maintain hand orientation and opening. The left view shows an open case top: the exterior wall blocks the previous low view, but does not establish that an above-rim robot-held inspection is impossible.

first_step.action: Bounded no-contact open-hand retreat with wrist-image reacquisition
first_step.direction_reference: Toward the open case top and away from the visible PCB, not downward alongside the exterior wall. Determine the corresponding robot motion using the calibrated camera/robot relationship; no world target is inferred here.
stop_conditions: Stop immediately if either finger appears to approach the PCB, cooler, motherboard, or case rim rather than separate from it.
Stop on any apparent card motion, unexpected resistance, or loss of a usable view of nearby obstacles.
Stop before moving if the withdrawal direction cannot be distinguished from a direction that crosses the card or rim.
At 10 mm total displacement, hold and reassess even if the shroud remains hidden; do not extend the retreat automatically.

visible_risks: The right fingertip is visually close to the PCB corner; depth separation is unresolved.
PCB components and the exposed gold connector are unsuitable default pinch targets.
The cooler/shroud is largely hidden by the PCB in the current wrist view.
The case rim and motherboard constrain withdrawal; an open top alone does not certify the hand's swept clearance.
uncertainty: This inspection addresses interior self-occlusion and fingertip occlusion, not the already-failed exterior-wall viewpoint. A short retreat may improve the edge view without revealing an opposing shroud face. Neither clearance nor object dimensions are established. Subsequent opposing-jaw geometry may use an explicitly justified hidden opposing face, but the current image does not yet provide a sufficiently identifiable mechanical contact patch.
